english.title: Purchase / acquire rocket / ammunition - military equipment
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without the authority of the Secretary of State, purchased or acquired

(A)_[a rocket,]_
(B)_[ammunition,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF ROCKET OR AMMUNITION..), not falling within section 5(1)(c) of the Firearms Act 1968, and which consisted in or incorporated a missile designed to explode on or immediately before impact and which was for military use
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(1A)(b) of, and Schedule 6 to, the Firearms Act 1968.

english.notes:
(i) See also offence wordings: H1815 and H1817.
(ii) For the possession of other (non military) prohibited ammunition see H1811, H1812, H1813 and H2237.
(iii) Section 5(7)(a) of the Firearms Act 1968 provides that a rocket is to be taken to be for military use if it is designed to be capable of being used with a military weapon.
(iv) Section 5A of the Act contains exemptions.
(v) On conviction for this offence, the court can order the forfeiture or disposal of any firearm or ammunition and cancellation of any firearm certificate or shot gun certificate, and any firearm or ammunition subject of such order may be seized or detained by a constable (section 52).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.

Time limit for prosecutions:
